items.title: AI tool designed and integrated into hospital workflows to classify skin lesions
items.excerpt: University of Alicante and Sant Joan d'Alacant University Hospital launched MEL-IA, an AI system that automates skin-lesion classification inside real hospital workflows.

items.title: AI model achieves 89% accuracy in identifying arrhythmia-related abnormalities in atrial tissue
items.excerpt: Technical University of Valencia researchers built a graph neural network that localizes atrial cardiomyopathy tissue damage from non-invasive electrical recordings with 89% accuracy; validated so far on simulated data.

items.title: Autonomous AI could create capacity for thousands more dermatology appointments, real-world study finds
items.excerpt: A real-world study of 8,391 patients found autonomous AI could free roughly 8,500 dermatology appointments over 16 months by safely discharging benign cases, with over 98% sensitivity for invasive melanoma.

items.title: AI chatbots give us a narrow slice of knowledge: Researchers warn of 'knowledge collapse'
items.excerpt: University of Copenhagen researchers found AI chatbots deliver significantly less diverse information than Google search across 155 topics, warning of 'knowledge collapse' as models train on AI text.

items.title: Does the gender pay gap extend to AI? Research finds female AI agents 'paid' less
items.excerpt: University of Limerick research finds workplace gender bias can be replicated in interactions with AI, with female-presenting AI agents 'paid' less.

items.title: The tests that grade AI may be getting it wrong
items.excerpt: Stanford researchers analyzed 56 widely used AI benchmarks and found major measurement inconsistencies, including safety benchmarks that degrade across languages, arguing for measurement-science methods.

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Psychologists apply attachment theory, the framework for people's most significant relationships, to explain how and why humans bond with AI companions.

items.title: How AI helped bring an ancient tomb dating to before the Roman empire back to life
items.excerpt: Pairing artificial intelligence with acoustic technology helped researchers reveal an Etruscan tomb in a new light.

items.title: The effects of an 'algorithmic monoculture' depend on the details
items.excerpt: MIT research finds that many firms using a single hiring algorithm, so-called algorithmic monoculture, is less harmful to job seekers than prior work suggested, depending on the details.

items.title: Don't be fooled—LLMs don't reason
items.excerpt: Ten years after AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol, today's AI still isn't tapping into the search-and-planning machinery that made that win possible, the essay argues.

items.title: Opinion: Will Claude ever win a Nobel Prize for medicine?
items.excerpt: On Nobel week, an op-ed asks whether some or all Nobels may one day go to Claude, ChatGPT or their successors rather than human scientists.

items.title: Detecting forever chemicals—with yeast and AI
items.excerpt: Researchers pair engineered yeast biosensors with AI analysis to detect PFAS 'forever chemicals' in samples.

items.title: Self-driving lab automates semiconductor ink synthesis and thin-film characterization
items.excerpt: KIT's Energy Materials Acceleration Platform (E-MAP) robotically synthesizes semiconductor inks and characterizes thin films, using AI for data analysis and experiment optimization.

items.title: Want to use AI to improve your work? Have it disagree with you
items.excerpt: A study of 45 knowledge workers found that prompting AI to challenge their ideas, rather than accepting its output, improved work quality and preserved critical thinking.

items.title: X-Rays and AI Reveal How Spacecraft Heat Shields Burn in Real Time
items.excerpt: Berkeley Lab researchers combined X-ray imaging with AI analysis to watch spacecraft heat-shield material ablate in real time.

items.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
items.excerpt: Mathematicians are facing AI's sudden shift with grief, anger and a search for fresh ideas: 'If we don't adapt, there's just no more math in 50 years.'

items.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy
items.excerpt: UCLA researchers built an optical AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos at once, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy.

items.title: MIT's tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
items.excerpt: A new AI control system gives MIT's insect-scale flying robot insect-like agility, boosting speed about 450% and enabling 10 consecutive somersaults.

items.title: AIDAQ 2026: AI is Now a staple of The Quantum story
items.excerpt: At Bitkom's AI, Data & Quantum Summit in Berlin, AI kept turning up inside quantum computing work, from error correction to control.

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for monitoring and protecting wildlife around the world.

items.title: Your Brain on AI: Why We Must Choose What We Outsource
items.excerpt: GenAI delivers the shortcuts our brains love, but overreliance has a cognitive cost; the piece outlines what we lose when we outsource thinking.
